title: Token-level observability: metrics, dashboards, tracing improvements, and alert tuning
author: Priya Patel
description:
Summary: Add token-level observability across the serving runtime and console dashboards, improve trace context propagation for end-to-end latency attribution, and tune alerts for cost/latency regressions. Motivation: customers increasingly ask for per-token cost/latency breakdowns to diagnose regressions and attribute cost. This PR adds low-overhead token metrics, example Grafana dashboards, updated Otel spans and logs, and adjusted alert thresholds with runbook suggestions.

What this changes: 1) Runtime metrics: new Prometheus counters and histograms emitted from the serving runtime (token_emit_total, token_emit_latency_seconds_bucket, token_cache_hits_total, token_generation_cost_units) with labels: model, route, customer_tier, quantization_profile. 2) Tracing: ensure KV cache and batching boundaries propagate trace/span IDs; added semantic span names for batch_affinity and kv_cache_lookup. 3) Logging: structured log fields for token counts and cost estimates (token_count, estimated_cost_usd) emitted at INFO for request summary. 4) Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard JSON (observability-pack/dashboards/token-level.json) with panels for token throughput, p50/p95/p99 token latency, cost per 1k tokens, and heatmaps by model and route. 5) Alerts: tuned alert rules to reduce noisy firing (alerting/alert_rules.yaml) with two new alerts: TokenLatencyRegression and TokenCostSpike, plus updated severity and runbooks. 6) Console: small console UI tweaks to show token-level breakdown in request details and link to the dashboards.

Checklist: - [x] Add runtime metrics and tests - [x] Add tracing/span tests (unit + integration) - [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON and example PromQL queries - [x] Add alert rules and runbooks - [x] Update console UI to surface token breakdown - [x] Update docs with examples and migration notes

Notes on performance: metrics are emitted with sampling and aggregated labels to avoid cardinality explosion. The runtime metric emission is guarded behind a per-customer flag (default off for low-tier customers) and the code path uses async batching to avoid blocking hot loops.

Related: ENG-4523 (observability epic), SUP-1284 (customer report showing token cost spike), PRs: pr-18421-token-level-observability-and-dashboards.json, pr-18930-token-level-observability-dashboard-alert-tuning.json

review_comments: Ethan Zhang (Reviewer): Can you explain the label cardinality limits? We need assurance this won't cause high series explosion for customers with many routes.

Priya Patel (Author): We cap dynamic labels; only model, route (hashed to 8 chars), customer_tier, and quantization_profile are used. We also default the feature flag off for low-tier customers. Added documentation and tests demonstrating series counts in observability-pack/queries/token_promql.md.

Ava Chen (Reviewer): Alert thresholds look reasonable but I'd like a short cooldown window to avoid flapping during deploys. Also please add a noise-reduction heuristic for the first 10 minutes after a rollout.
Priya Patel (Author): Added cooldown (5m for P2, 30m for P1) and heuristic to ignore spikes with deployment label for 10m. See alert_rules.yaml lines updated.

Miguel Torres (Reviewer): Integration test failed initially on CI due to missing trace context in the batch path. After your fix to span_propagation it's now covered by tests. Please squash the fix-up commit before merge.
Priya Patel (Author): Fixed and squashed; updated commit history. Thanks for catching this.
ci_checks: ci/integration: initially failed (trace propagation test), rerun -> pass
merge_details: merge_note: Squashed commits and added small changelog entry. All CI green at time of merge.
release_notes: Observability: Added token-level metrics, tracing improvements for precise latency attribution, Grafana token-level dashboard, tuned alerting for token latency and cost spikes, and console UI to surface token breakdowns. Default feature flag is off for low-tier customers. See docs/observability/token-level.md for migration and runbooks.
notes: Performance and safety: metrics emission is sampled and guarded by per-customer flags to control cardinality.
Rollout plan: feature flag rollout to 10% of customers for 48h, then 50% for 24h, then global onboarding. Watch TokenLatencyRegression alert during rollout.
Follow-ups: add aggregated daily cost reports by model (ENG-4591), and add Cost Attribution API (ENG-4620).
